candidate.title: 3’NT / method
candidate.scope: The single 3′NT (3′ end of nascent transcripts) workflow in the assigned Illumina poster row: isolate the transcriptome complex, retain an insoluble chromatin complex, extract associated RNA, and convert it to the depicted cDNA endpoint. Inventory of the complete crop: the upper CAGE and DeepCAGE rows, lower NET-Seq row (including its immunoprecipitation icon), and clipped chemical end-group panel at the right are neighboring context without a connecting route into 3′NT. They are not alternative targets of this card. The 3′NT row has one linear route, no depicted split, pooling or alternative. Its RNA/Cap labels, complex attachment, insoluble fraction and cDNA endpoint are retained. Catalogue statements about cap enrichment and modified NET-Seq library preparation clarify the biological target but do not add unshown operations. This describes the supported schematic, not all implementations of nascent-RNA sequencing.

evidence.quote:

purified RNAPII-chromatin complex and enriched for mRNA by selecting for strands with 5’ 7-methylguanosine caps. cDNA

unknowns.question: How does the implementation preserve the original RNA 3′ terminus through priming, adapter construction and cDNA recovery so that a sequenced end identifies the polymerase position? The figure gives only reverse transcription and cDNA, while the catalogue reports the end-based RNAPII readout. The supplied primary abstract supports nucleotide-resolution position mapping but supplies no library-end mechanism. Primary methods or an end-resolved library schematic would resolve this interface.

Where and how is the 5′-cap enrichment reported by the matching catalogue page performed relative to RNA extraction and cDNA production? The drawing displays Cap on complex-bound RNA but depicts no cap-selection transformation. Primary methods evidence would be needed to place that unshown selection, and cap depiction alone does not establish selection efficiency.
